title: One member account may store about twice the whole free database in its workout copy
what: Anyone who signs in with Google gets a server copy that is capped only by row count (30,000) and by size per row (32 KB). Together that is close to 1 GB for a single account, while the whole free database is 500 MB and is shared with every gym. Nothing caps the total bytes per member or how fast one account may write. One damaged or misused phone could fill the database and stop every gym's desk from saving.
expected: Each member's copy has a total size cap sized to the plan (a few MB is years of real training) and a pace limit, so one account can never fill the shared database.
who: every gym, through any one member account
fix_line: Add a total size cap per member copy and a write pace limit on the server

title: A very long workout is silently left out of the saved copy while Settings says everything is saved
what: A workout or other item bigger than the copy's size limit per item is skipped and only noted in the developer log. It never joins the waiting count, so the backup line in Settings says the workouts are saved. On a new phone that workout is missing.
expected: The member is told that one workout could not be saved to the account, and it is shown as not saved, or it is split so it fits.
fix_line: Show a not-saved line for items over the size limit, or split them

title: No early warning before a member's saved copy is full
what: The member only hears about the copy limit once it is reached and new workouts stop being saved. Neither the member nor MettleUp gets a warning as the copy gets close to the limit.
expected: A gentle note to the member, and a count for MettleUp, when a copy passes about 80% of its limit.
fix_line: Warn at about 80% full, and list near-full copies in HQ
